blockers.description: BUG A (real defect — should be fixed before sign-off): the sidebar's board list does not scroll independently of the page. Confirmed via browser_evaluate against the running dev server: nav.scrollHeight === nav.clientHeight (1078px) regardless of viewport height (tested at 700px and 900px), and nav's overflow-y computes to 'visible'. The whole page grows/scrolls instead of the list alone, pushing the pinned theme-toggle/Hide-Sidebar controls below the viewport fold — reachable only by scrolling the entire page, not the panel. This violates the plan's own must_have: "the list scrolls while the brand mark and pinned controls stay put."
blockers.workaround: Needs a real fix (likely: the list's scroll container needs min-h-0 on its flex ancestor and overflow-y-auto on itself, so it can shrink below its content height inside the fixed-height nav panel) — not something to talk around. Screenshots were sent to the user via SendUserFile this session (02-09-desktop-short-viewport.png) but not committed to the repo.

blockers.description: BUG B (disclosed/foreseeable consequence of the Option B decision, not a coding mistake, but should be explicitly recorded as a known limitation rather than silently accepted): at 375px viewport, document.documentElement.scrollWidth (426px) exceeds clientWidth (360px) — real horizontal page overflow with a visible scrollbar, because the fixed-300px sidebar plus content column no longer fits at mobile width. This is the mechanical, foreseeable result of deferring the mobile treatment to plan 02-11 (Option B) — it was not explicitly called out as a consequence when the user picked Option B earlier in this session.
blockers.workaround: Recommend recording as an explicitly accepted, temporary limitation in 02-09-SUMMARY.md (resolved when 02-11 lands the real mobile treatment) rather than trying to fix it in this plan — fixing it properly means building part of the Option B/mobile-overlay work this plan deliberately deferred. Screenshot sent to user via SendUserFile (02-09-mobile-375.png), not committed to the repo.

decisions.decision: A first continuation attempt via SendMessage to the original executor agent (a96fc08d135d037f3) failed — its worktree no longer existed on disk when it tried to resume
decisions.rationale: Claude Code's isolation="worktree" tears the worktree down once an Agent() invocation returns, even at a mid-plan checkpoint — SendMessage resumes the agent's conversation but not the filesystem it was standing on. No commits were lost (0/4 tasks done at that point), but the lesson: continuations for worktree-isolated executors must always be a fresh Agent() call with the resolved state folded into the prompt, never a SendMessage expecting the same worktree to still exist. The second attempt (fresh Agent(), decision pre-resolved in the prompt) worked correctly and its worktree (agent-a9d0c82a3b179a474) is still alive as of this handoff.
